title: A merged PR is not permission to delete a working tree (gh-435, gh-467)
body:
Closes #435. Closes #467.

## What was wrong

`fr`'s isolation gc reaped a workspace the moment its PR read `MERGED`, and the teardown it
called guarded exactly one thing: an **open** PR. Everything else about that workspace —
uncommitted edits, a commit that never left the machine — was deleted with no prompt, no
warning, no stash, no salvage copy.

The shape of the defect was visible in one file. The **speculative** classifier,
`_merged_by_content`, refused to act on a dirty tree. The **authoritative** path,
`pr_state == "MERGED"`, did not look at all. Confidence about the *classification* was
silently read as confidence about the *working tree*.

This repo's own integration suite had pinned the bug as correct behaviour:
`test_hostworktree_full_lifecycle_no_docker_base_untouched` wrote an untracked `scratch.txt`
into a workspace and then asserted a plain `down(force=False)` removed it. The guard turned
that test red — the clearest single statement of #435 in the codebase.

## What changed

`Target._reap_hazard(state)` — a pure query — runs in `_down_worktree_tail`, immediately
after the OPEN-PR guard and before any destructive step. That is the single narrow waist
every reap already passes through (`fr isolation down`, `down --all`, `down --worktree`, and
both of gc's reap branches, which get there via `down(state, force=False)`), shared by the
devcontainer and host-worktree modes. Three hazards, local check first so the free one
short-circuits before any network:

| Hazard | Trigger | Remedy offered |
|---|---|---|
| `dirty-worktree` | `git status --porcelain` non-empty — tracked **and** untracked | commit or stash |
| `unlanded-content` | a changed file not on `origin/<default>` | push the branch |
| `unverifiable` | the query itself failed (status, fetch, or comparison) | fix connectivity/history |

gc reports a refusal as `skipped` with the hazard's own text — never `reap-failed`, which
reads as breakage — and `--dry-run` asks the same question the live path enforces, so a
preview never promises an action the live run refuses.

`--force` remains the single deliberate escape and now covers all three guards. It still
never skips the #354 teardown post-condition verification.

### Two design notes worth reading

**#467's own wording would not have fixed #467.** It asked to refuse "when the branch is
ahead of its remote". GitHub's auto-delete-branch means that after a squash-merge there is
usually no remote branch left: `@{upstream}` does not resolve and the check goes silent in
exactly the shape that fired the issue. The guard asks the content question against
`origin/<default>` instead — squash-safe, and it catches a commit **pushed** after the merge
(the #320 orphan) for free.

**`verify_merge` is the wrong reuse**, and the code says so at the call site. It is fetch +
`branch_changes_present` + `self._pr(state)`, and that third call shells out to
`gh`/`glab`/`tea` — which gc already did one line earlier to classify the workspace. Reusing
it would buy a second host-CLI round trip per candidate on a host-wide sweep, then discard
its `verified` field, which the PR-less path can never satisfy.

## Operator gates

```
brainstorm: operator gate answered by the operator
```

Four decisions were put to the operator in one batch and are recorded in the spec journal
(`fr journal render --scope spec --slug 2026-09-20-isolation-reap-data-loss-guards
--section decisions`):

- **d1** — dirty means any `git status --porcelain` output, tracked and untracked alike.
  #435 floated ignoring untracked files; its own lost work included a newly authored
  (therefore untracked) phase file, so that carve-out would not have saved it.
- **d2** — the #467 check is content-based against `origin/<default>`, not `@{upstream}`.
- **d3** — no salvage ref; refusal is the whole fix. **Plus an addition the operator made:**
  `--force` is operator-requested-**and-informed** only. That lands as skill prose (below),
  because no test can detect "an agent decided by itself".
- **d4** — the post-merge Test Plan: reproduce both issues live, then a host-wide dry-run
  sweep.

## Findings raised and fixed in review

Every phase was reviewed before the next was dispatched. Eight findings, all fixed with
tests, all recorded in the plan journal.

| # | Finding |
|---|---|
| f1 | The shared message helper hardcoded one remedy clause for three hazards — "Commit or stash them" has no referent when `git status` itself failed. `remedy` is now per-hazard and required. |
| f2 | The `--force` line overstated the damage. **Verified against real git:** `git worktree remove --force` leaves the branch and its commits intact, so #435 (uncommitted, unrecoverable) and #467 (local-only commit, branch survives) are not equally severe. The message now says what `--force` does. An operator who believes it deletes their commits will not use it — a false refusal by another route. |
| f3 | The content guard made a repo with **no `origin` remote** un-reapable without `--force`. `fr isolation up` supports remote-less repos deliberately ("no origin remote — basing on local HEAD"), and `--force` is the one lever d3 forbids an agent reaching for unprompted. A local `git remote get-url origin` now separates "no remote configured" from "fetch failed". This was also the root cause of a four-file test-fixture churn that had been absorbed as test debt. |
| f4 | `_reap_hazard` could raise (`branch_changes_present` raises on unrelated histories). `_gc_one`'s `if dry_run:` arms sit **outside** their `try`, so once phase 3 called the guard from there, an escaping exception would have aborted the entire host-wide sweep — breaking gc's documented "one failed workspace never aborts the sweep" invariant. Closed at the source before phase 3 shipped it. |
| f5 | `gc --dry-run` resolved the **sweeping** repo's default branch, not the workspace's. gc is host-wide, so a `master` repo swept from a `main` one previewed `would-skip` for a workspace the live run reaps — the exact preview/live divergence the dry-run change exists to remove. The live path was never affected; it builds a sibling Target first, the idiom `_merged_by_content` already uses. |
| f6 | `down --all` inlined multi-line refusal reasons into its one-line summary, putting a `; ` separator mid-sentence and burying the sentinel count at the tail of a paragraph. Caught by printing the real output, not by reading the code. |
| f7 | The 120-line skill cap was met partly by **deleting content** — an explanatory parenthetical and an entire third status-line option with its command — while reporting "no content lost". `test_skill_validation`'s hyphenated-word docstring already documents this exact trap. Both fragments restored verbatim; verified by `difflib` against the pre-change file that nothing present before is absent after. |
| f8 | The new prose tripwire's docstring claimed to match stable phrases and asserted literal wording; the rewrap in f7 broke it on a pronoun and a verb conjugation within the same PR. Now regex on semantic markers, verified non-vacuous. |

## The obligation code cannot enforce

Per **d3**, `plugins/super-fr/skills/fr-isolation/SKILL.md` now states that an agent must
never reach for `--force` on its own initiative — only after the operator asks — and must
first name what would be destroyed. The clause **says plainly that nothing enforces it**:
this repo's convention is that standing rules are enforced by tests, so an unenforced one
announces itself rather than borrowing the credibility of the enforced ones. A tripwire pins
the prose existing in all three shipped copies; it cannot pin the obligation being followed.

## Acceptance matrix

Four rows added at brainstorm, all now `ci`:

| Row | Claim |
|---|---|
| `isolation-reap-preserves-uncommitted` | uncommitted work in a merged workspace survives every reap path |
| `isolation-reap-preserves-unlanded` | work not on `origin/<default>` survives every reap path |
| `isolation-reap-force-escape` | `--force` still works, and still verifies the #354 post-condition |
| `isolation-reap-guards-dont-strand` | a clean, landed workspace is **still reaped**, and `--dry-run` predicts the live outcome |

The fourth is the defence against this change's real risk: a guard that never reaps replaces
a data-loss bug with a nagging one. `fr acceptance check`: 128 rows OK (106 `ci`, 18
`skipped`, 4 `not-implemented` — all pre-existing and unrelated). No rows were added
mid-flight beyond the four born with the spec.

## Explainers

`docs/explainers/fr-isolation.html` describes the sweep ("every `up`/`down` fires a detached,
best-effort sweep"; "teardown re-checks the actual post-condition"). **Nothing this change
does makes that false.** It is nevertheless owed a sentence, and cannot get one: it is one of
the two published pages with **no committed `.md` source** (`explainers-currency.md`, known
gap 1), so regeneration is impossible rather than merely skipped. Recording which of the two
it is, per that rule.

## Version

**4.8.0 → 4.9.0 (minor).** A refusal that did not exist before is user-visible mandatory
behaviour, plus a shipped skill edit — not a patch-level fix.

## Verification

```
ruff check packages/ tests/ scripts/   All checks passed!
mypy (4 packages)                      Success: no issues found in 138 source files
sync-opencode.py --check               .opencode/ mirrors are in sync.
sync-hermes.py --check                 .hermes/ mirrors are in sync.
fr validate artifacts                  33 artifact(s) checked — all structurally valid.
fr acceptance check                    128 rows OK
bump-version.py --check                ok — versions agree (4.9.0)
pytest (full, coverage gate)           1 failed, 3328 passed, 80 skipped
                                       Total coverage: 91.73% (gate 75%)
```

The one failure is `tests/unit/test_workflow_check.py::test_cli_all_fails_when_nothing_is_discoverable`
(#463/#489), pre-existing and untouched by this branch — recorded as the baseline in phase 1
and independently re-confirmed three times. A note for reviewers: this machine runs ~10
concurrent isolation worktrees sharing one global `uv tool install` target, which produced
two separate spurious failures during this work (both investigated and ruled out, journalled
as `p3-global-uv-tool-install-collision` and `p4-basetemp-path-length-false-positive`). A
single green local run here is weaker evidence than it looks; CI is the arbiter.

## Test Plan — post-merge, operator-driven

Verbatim from the spec, per **d4**:

14. Stage a merged workspace, dirty it, run `fr isolation gc` — confirm the refusal message
    and that the directory survives.
15. Stage a merged workspace holding a local-only commit — same.
16. `fr isolation gc --dry-run` across the real host — confirm genuinely-merged clean
    workspaces still report `would-reap`. This is the false-refusal check; nothing offline
    can stand in for it.

## Artifacts

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-isolation-reap-data-loss-guards-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-isolation-reap-data-loss-guards/`
- Journals: `docs/superpowers/journals/{specs,plans}/2026-09-20-isolation-reap-data-loss-guards.md`

## Third-party privacy

No hostname, org, repo or username outside `derio-net` appears in this branch's code, tests,
fixtures, journals, commit messages or this body. All fixtures use synthetic names.

---

## Ready

- **CI green** on `76bbcaa` — lint, typecheck, test, matrix, validate-artifacts,
  opencode-plugin-test, version-sync, version-bump-required all pass.
- **Review pass recorded** by the operator.
- **No commits since** that review pass.

Note on the local baseline above: the `test` job passes on CI, so
`test_workflow_check.py::test_cli_all_fails_when_nothing_is_discoverable` (#463/#489) is a
**local-environment** failure, not a repo-wide one. That is a sharper statement than this
branch started with, and it corroborates the concurrency caveat in Verification.
